892:513. **Which run-time class carries each built-in type of the one library on the compiled path, for the types that P-178 does not cover?** The rehearsal's question, the plan review's, and question 1 of the carriers' review. A carrier is the JVM class whose instances are a built-in type's values, as `FZZ32` for the prelude's `trait ZZ32`. Answered for the five number types `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `ZZ`, `NN64` and `RR64` by his decision of 2026-11-16 (P-178; the review's way D): each is one `value object` under its own name, no trait stays above it, and compiled code can hold its value as a bare JVM `int`, `long` or `double` (P-17); `NN32` and `RR32` already have that form. Not open, corrected on 2026-11-16 after the curator asked whether these types had not been discussed before: `value object Boolean` and `value object Char` are objects with no trait in the one library, the form that P-178 gives the numbers, and stay so; the Java-backed traits are decided, `JavaBufferedWriter` and `JavaBufferedReader` by P-164 (his "(b) it is." of 2026-11-06: at the switch-over the run-time classes implement the one library's traits) and the two array stores by P-169 (the Fable judgement that he took on 2026-11-07, with his choice of the slot API on 2026-11-08). For `String` nothing is his to decide, and no new probe is due (corrected again on 2026-11-16, after he said that the record had not been searched; the scout's fourth pass, and the reports themselves). The shape is fixed by his words and decisions: the coordinator's line of 2026-11-05 18:28Z, which he did not contest, "how Fortress strings live on the JVM, the team already decided ... That design stays; nothing on the table reopens it"; his words of 2026-11-07 05:42Z, strings are "user extensible/modifiable reference types", with room "to slip specialized implementation under String trait, like the CatString does"; P-168 and P-171. The work is done in three places: `reviews/carriers-ways-2026-11-13.md`, "On `String`" under each way (`String` is an interface, `FlatString`'s class holds a `java.lang.String`, a wrapper casts a helper's `String` parameter; "This is the same in every way"), and "the two libraries agree"; the rehearsal's wall W2, built in scratch and run (`compile-ladder/plan-31/probes/switch-rehearsal.md`); probe Y's second set of run-time classes (F-353). Left for a builder, with the merge of P-178: the form that gives `FlatString`'s class while it stays an object, the same work as for `Boolean`, `Char`, `NN32`, `RR32` and the merged numbers; F-322's two readings of a helper's `String` parameter; ropes and a program's own `String` compiled, which wait on other rows. For his review at its default: item 466, a string object's ilk keeps `FlatString`. Also the planner's, not his: whether the class of a native object is written by hand over a generated springboard, or by the code generator over a hand-written payload class (the review's way C, forms 1 and 2). The team's sources do not point to one way (F-359, F-360).
934:572. **After the merge, where is the rung placed for the self-typed order traits' bodies that fail verification at an object instance?** Finding 1 of climb batch 31's post-batch review, with gather.1 of its gather, review.1 of its merged-diff review and judge-review.1 of the review's judge (row 1051), and rows 1050 and 1052 of its rung K. Measured on the merged tree: a self-typed trait's default body `mx(self, other: T): T = if lt(other, self) then self else other end`, with an object that extends the trait directly, compiles and dies when it runs, 'VerifyError: Bad return type'; rung K casts a returned `self`, and no arm of a conditional. By reading, not run: the one library's `StandardTotalOrder` writes `MIN`, `MAX` and `MINMAX` in that shape (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:291-294`), and after the merge each built-in integer type is a `value object` directly below it. Beside it stand a closure that returns `self` (row 1050) and a default body that calls a method on a value of the self parameter, which dies with `ClassCircularityError` (row 1052).
957:512. **Which order of the remaining work: the whole switch-over first, or the model's slice first, with one build that serves both libraries?** Finding A of the plan review, as it stands after the rehearsal's end, and the first question of probe Y. The rehearsal met two kinds of wall: walls that a test compiled against the prelude can show today, 11 to 15 rungs under either order, and walls that only a tree switched onto the one library shows (F-352). In the first order (A1), the walls that only the switch shows, the move of the 1,907 compiled tests and the prelude's deletion are one landing that cannot be gated in parts. In the second (A2), the compile command selects the one library beside the prelude, a second set of the run time's value classes serves it, and those walls are met one at a time on `main`; the prelude lives until the end. P-33's order of the phases and P-85's word that the array work comes after the switch-over stand until he decides; the one library (P-37) is not in question.

At a trait type the check refuses it (row 785). The guard of the check's point B2 is the coordinator's decision between the go and the launch: `tests/GenericBesidePlainObjectNoReturnTypeWalk.fss` passes, and the invalid form of such a pair loads. After the merge such pairs over the five number types move from refused to loaded unjudged.
1066:570. **Walk loads the invalid pair of a generic declaration beside a plain one over an arrow type (row 1049); told.** X.skeptic.4 of climb batch 31's rung X. The skeptic wrote no gated test, since rung V edited that load check the same night; the gather's run on the merged tree shows the pair loading still, so an expected-failure walk test can now be written.
1222:563. **The natural spelling of a search, and a numeral as the value of an atomic expression, wait for their rows; told.** L.worker.3 and L.skeptic.3 of climb batch 31's rung L (row 340), and row 1043 of its rung A. `exit found with i` beside a last `-1` does not compile until row 340 is repaired; a program binds the number to a typed variable first. The checker carries no declared type into the body of an atomic expression, so a numeral there is refused or fails verification; `atomic do ... end` runs (row 1043). By P-50 and P-173 the numeral that ends a label block at a declared number type takes that type in place, so the first case is P-50's spelling unbuilt; it is filed under row 340's crash.
1878:544. **Are the record's forks R1, R2, S2, C2, B1, N1 to N4 and D2 kept as taken?** The forks of climb batch 32's record that have no item of their own (`coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-32.md`, section 3, "Forks the batch takes"), each at its default. R1: one run of seven rungs. R2: row 758 in the batch, as rung C's second step. S2: `f(x)^T` stays a static error on both paths (row 144).
